en.html:
One week had passed since disaster overtook Shishiku Ootori, Lord of Sasagawa. Days of upheaval? No. Compared with what came before, one could call them a standstill.

In Aizu, hostilities had not begun.

Rokuhara had lost every leader who possessed both standing and actual strength. At last it could no longer play one of the two leading parts in the affairs of the day. The occupation army, meanwhile, had lost the point of taking action. Strength it had. A use for that strength it did not. It had been pushed into watching and waiting.

People's heads were growing quite numb from one incident after another. Their mouths, however, continued discussing everything at full volume.

Who had cut Rokuhara's last lifeline?

At first, most said it must have been an assassin from GHQ. Then another story gradually spread, carrying the qualification that survivors from the Ootori main residence had supplied it: the eldest daughter of the previous head, whom Shishiku had killed, had taken her revenge.

Soon the two explanations were twisted together. The occupation army had helped the Ootori princess kill Shishiku. Settled. There were fragments of truth in it, and fragments standing very near the truth; the conclusion, of course, was wrong.

Arre, two rumors had married and produced a fact. Witnesses? Those were the guests at the wedding; nobody was waiting for them to arrive before feeding everybody. One story supplied the killer, the other supplied the motive, and now the public could sleep peacefully with a complete explanation. Whether it explained what had happened was a separate, rather fussy objection.

The very people who wanted Shishiku Ootori alive were the occupation forces. If necessary, they might almost have sent guards to keep him that way. They wanted a decisive battle with Rokuhara, and the last great commander capable of holding the shogunate army together was indispensable to that purpose.

Shishiku, too, had understood this. That was precisely why he could afford not to divert fighting strength to his own protection. What had happened fell outside everybody's calculations.

Still, depending on how matters developed, the rumor might yet serve the occupation army. If the tale of revenge became a stirring story in the public mind, GHQ would become its unseen benefactor. Prestige would come without their having done the deed.

Perhaps people might even grow ready to accept them as the real rulers of Yamato. GHQ's watchful silence—Lieutenant Colonel Cannon's silence—surely meant waiting for this as well, not merely sitting with folded hands.

Yamato needed a ruler in any case. After confusion upon confusion, the conviction that this ruler must not be the foreign occupation army was already fading from people's minds.

篠川公方大鳥獅子吼の遭難から一週間。
　それは激動の日々ではなかった。むしろ、それ以前
に比べれば停滞とさえ云える時間であった。

　会津において、戦端は開かれなかったのである。

　六波羅は地位と実力を兼ね備える領袖をすべて失い、
遂に時勢の一方の主役たり得なくなった。
　進駐軍は行動の意義を無くし、力は有りながら静観
する以外にない立場へ追いやられた。

　人々は打ち続く事変にいい加減頭を麻痺させつつ、
それでも声高に噂し合った。

　何者が、六波羅の最後の命脈を絶ったのか――

　初め、多くの者はＧＨＱの刺客に違いないと語った。
　それから次第に、大鳥本邸の生き残りからの伝聞と
いう但し書き付きで、別の噂が広まっていった。――
獅子吼に殺された大鳥先代の長女が復讐を遂げた、と。

　二つの見解はやがて縒り合わされ、進駐軍が大鳥の
姫を<ruby>援<rt>たす</rt></ruby>けて獅子吼を討たせたという形に落ち着いた。
　それは断片的な真実と真実に近いものを含みつつ、
無論、結論としては誤っている。

　大鳥獅子吼に、何となれば護衛を派遣したく思う程
存命していて欲しかったのは他ならぬ進駐軍である。
　六波羅との決戦を欲する彼らにとって、幕軍を取り
まとめる最後の大将帥は必要不可欠の人材だった。

　獅子吼とてその点を見切っていたからこそ、身辺の
防備に戦力を割かずにいられたのである。
　全ては彼らの計算の枠外で行われた事だった。

　しかしながらこの噂は、状況の推移如何では、進駐
軍に利する見込みもあったろう。
　つまり仇討ち話が美談として巷間に浸透するなら、
ＧＨＱは影の立役者となり、声望を得られる。

　彼らが大和の支配実権を握っても良しとする土壌が
あるいは形成されるかもしれなかった。
　ＧＨＱ――キャノン中佐の静観には、ただ手を<ruby>拱<rt>こまね</rt></ruby>く
ばかりでなく、それを待つ意味もあったに違いない。

　どのみち大和に統治者は必要なのだ。
　混乱に次ぐ混乱の中、その統治者が外部勢力の進駐
軍であってはならないとする意識は、人々の脳裏から
既に失われつつあった。

en.html:
But now another factor entered the calculation.

The Imperial Court in Kyoto.

Such efficiency from the imperial family and its supporters, one would think this possibility had been anticipated. First, an understanding with the Muromachi Tandai, Rokuhara's regional administration in the Kinai. Mutual cooperation, promised.

With that behind them, negotiations began with the Dazaifu in Kyushu and the northern Chinjufu. Meanwhile, Kuniuji Ashikaga's proclamation as Lord General, left hanging after Fudaraku Castle collapsed, was formally postponed. Postponed, mind you.

ja.html:
しかしそこに、新たな<ruby>因子<rt>ファクター</rt></ruby>が参入する。

　京都朝廷である。

　あらかじめこうなる事を可能性として予期していた
かのような手際の良さで、皇族とその勢力は動いた。
　まず近畿における六波羅の出先機関である室町探題
と談合、相互協力の約束を取り付け、

　これを背景に九州の大宰府、北方の鎮守府とも交渉
を開始。
　その一方、普陀楽城崩壊で宙に浮いていた足利邦氏
への大将領宣下は、正式に<ruby>延期<rt>・・</rt></ruby>を決定する。

en.html:
The announcement explained that young Kuniuji could not be made to bear such heavy responsibilities under the present conditions. Until he came of age, a deputy would safeguard the position for him. Who this deputy would be had not yet been made clear. Not publicly, at any rate.

...Probably someone of imperial blood. Someone thoroughly acquainted with affairs throughout Kanto. Someone whose knowledge and cunning had probably guided the Court's present political moves from behind the scenes. Some such member of the imperial family would take the post, would they not?

Naam mat lo. No need to name anybody. Merely describe one particular gentleman from head to foot, leave a gentleman-shaped vacancy in the government, and wait to see what astonishing coincidence might fill it. Politics also had its little games for the whole family.

At the center, too, work began to rebuild the Two Departments and Eight Ministries. Legally, these were still Yamato's rightful government; in practice, they had been stripped of power and left an empty shell. The prime minister—the Minister of the Left—would apparently be chosen from the Five Regent Houses. The House of Peers and the House of Representatives also seemed likely to reopen.

The announcement explained that young Kuniuji could not be made to bear such heavy responsibilities under the present conditions. Until he came of age, a deputy would safeguard the position for him. Who this deputy would be had not yet been made clear. Not publicly, at any rate.

...Probably someone of imperial blood. Someone thoroughly acquainted with affairs throughout Kanto. Someone whose knowledge and cunning had probably guided the Court's present political moves from behind the scenes. Some such member of the imperial family would take the post, would they not?

Naam mat lo. No need to name anybody. Merely describe one particular gentleman from head to foot, leave a gentleman-shaped vacancy in the government, and wait to see what astonishing coincidence might fill it. Politics also had its little games for the whole family.

At the center, too, work began to rebuild the Two Departments and Eight Ministries. Legally, these were still Yamato's rightful government; in practice, they had been stripped of power and left an empty shell. The prime minister—the Minister of the Left—would apparently be chosen from the Five Regent Houses. The House of Peers and the House of Representatives also seemed likely to reopen.

ja.html:
若年の邦氏に現状下の重責を負わせ得ず、彼が成人
するまで代行の者を置いて地位を守らせる――と発表。
　誰がその代行を務めるのかについては、まだ明確に
されていない。表向きのところは。

　……おそらく皇族の人間が。
　それも関東一帯の情勢に詳しく、その知識と智謀に
よって今回の朝廷の政治行動を陰から指導もしたので
あろう<ruby>皇家の誰か<rt>・・・・・</rt></ruby>が、その任に就くのではないか。

　中央でも、法制上は大和の正当な政府でありながら
実権を奪われ形骸化していた、二官八省の再建に着手。
　首相つまり左大臣は五摂家から選ばれる模様である。
また、貴族院・衆議院両議会の閉鎖も解かれるようだ。

en.html:
All this activity reminded people that the government in Kyoto did, in fact, exist. A little expectation, a little trust began to grow. Even the leaderless remnants of Rokuhara were no exception. After all, the Six Guards had originally been institutions directly under the Court.

Very few openly objected to returning to the old arrangement and taking orders from Kyoto. With encouragement from the Muromachi Tandai, most of the remaining shogunate forces in Kanto were preparing to turn toward the capital and fall into line.

A movement was indeed taking shape: return Yamato to the days before Rokuhara, and restore peace and stability by its own strength. Naturally, this was not what the occupation army wanted. And what it did not want, it would presumably try to obstruct.

But the convenient villain it had relied on was gone. Before long it would have to decide: become the villain itself, become an invader, or accept a measure of compromise.

Would the storms of war rage across Yamato once more?
Would Yamato keep its independence?

............The answers, I—Kageaki Minato—would never know.

ja.html:
こうした朝廷の活性化は、人々に<ruby>首都政府<rt>キョウト</rt></ruby>の存在を
思い出させ、仄かな期待と信頼をも芽生えさせている。
　頭立つ者を失った六波羅残党もその例外とはならな
かった。元来が、六衛府は朝廷直属の機関なのだ。

　旧に復し、朝廷の指揮を仰ぐに、表立って抵抗感を
示す者はごく少なく……
　室町探題の働きかけもあり、関東の残存幕府勢力は
大半が京都の方角を向いて整列しようとしていた。

　大和を六波羅以前の時代へ<ruby>還<rt>かえ</rt></ruby>し、平和と安定を<ruby>独力<rt>・・</rt></ruby>
で取り戻す、そんな潮流が今確かに生まれている。
　……当然それは進駐軍の望むところではなく、望ま
ないからには妨害を試みてくるであろう。

　だが、進駐軍にとって都合の良い〝悪役〟はもはや
失われてしまった。
　彼らは遠からず、自ら悪役となり侵略者となるか、
それとも一定の妥協をするか、決断を迫られるだろう。

　大和の国土に、戦乱の嵐は再び吹き荒れるのか。
　大和の自立は、果たして守られるのか。

　…………その答えを、<ruby>湊斗景明<rt>おれ</rt></ruby>が知ることはない。
